column1: # Human-curated table of VER lemmas found in resources/LexiqueMixte.tsv that are
# NOT covered by resources/verbiste/verbs-fr.xml (i.e. absent from Verbiste's
# ~7,000-verb -> conjugation-template mapping), together with a manually reviewed
# conjugation-model assignment for each. See the "Undersampling-aware paradigm
# completion for sparse verb homophone groups" design plan for context.
# This table is the single source of truth for these verbs: util/completeVerbParadigms.py
# should look a verb up here (and fall back to Verbiste's own verbs-fr.xml lookup)
# rather than re-deriving any of this via prefix-stripping, elision rules, or other
# runtime heuristics -- those heuristics are deliberately NOT implemented in code
# (see conversation): every entry here was worked out by hand and should be edited
# STATUS remains scoped to what has been manually reviewed so far: the 18 -ir + 4
# -oir + 12 -re verbs from the residual Verbiste gap (34 total), plus the entries
# from that same gap review whose "lemma" looks like a LexiqueMixte lemma-extraction
# bug rather than a genuine missing verb. NOT YET COVERED: the ~478 leftover -er
# verbs (almost certainly regular, matchable by ending-pattern against Verbiste's
# existing -er templates without needing an exception here) and the ~205
# PROGRESS notes / conversation for that list) which still need individual
#   lemme            - the VER lemma as it appears in LexiqueMixte.tsv
#                      <template name="..."> ids) this lemma's paradigm should follow.
#                      Blank if status is skip_artifact, or if status is defective/
#                      needs_review and no template could be confidently assigned.
#   model_sibling    - a real, well-attested Verbiste-covered verb that already uses
#                      `template`, to use as the phonology/orthography splicing source
#       regular        confident this is a normal, fully-productive verb that simply
#                      happens to be missing from Verbiste; template should be trusted.
#       family_template confident based on a shared *irregular verb family* whose
#                      final string (not a strippable prefix) determines the template
#                      (e.g. reclure shares conclure/exclure's template even though
#                      bare "clure" isn't itself a Verbiste entry).
#       defective      genuinely defective/archaic verb: most of the paradigm does not
#                      exist in real French. Do NOT synthesize a full paradigm for
#                      these; only generate forms that are independently confirmed
#       needs_review   template guess is uncertain; needs a human linguist/native-
#                      speaker check before trusting it for row generation.
#       skip_artifact  this "lemma" is very likely a LexiqueMixte lemma-extraction bug
#                      (an inflected form, participle, or unrelated word wrongly
#                      stored as the lemma) rather than a real missing verb. Do not
#                      generate rows; consider fixing the source lexicon instead.

Plain -ir/-iss- verb; surprising it's absent from Verbiste at all, double check spelling before trusting.
Slang ("to say"); alt spelling of bonir, same template expected.
Alt spelling of bonnir, same template expected.
Plain -ir/-iss- verb ("to turn crimson").

Template matches "finir" per most references, but agonir is traditionally near-defective (mainly infinitive + "agonir d'injures"); cross-check against any attested corpus forms before generating a full paradigm.
re + souvenir with French re+s doubling (ressortir, resservir pattern); follows venir/souvenir's t:enir template exactly.
Survives only in "sans coup férir" and participle "féru"; no real paradigm to generate.

Archaic variant of advenir; defective, only 3rd-person forms attested (il avient). Possible lemma collision with the noun "avenir" (the future) -- verify against LexiqueMixte context before treating as this verb.
a + pâlir; pâlir itself should already be a Verbiste-covered fin:ir verb -- confirm pâlir's presence before relying on this.

The original motivating example (see design plan). "champir" is not itself a Verbiste entry, so this is a direct fin:ir assignment rather than a base-verb derivation; corpus frequency is 0 for all forms today.
Rare/impersonal ("to scorch", of plants); plausible fin:ir but not verified against attested forms.
Regional/dialectal; plausible fin:ir but not verified.
Likely a LexiqueMixte extraction bug: the real verb is probably "amocher" (-er), not "amochir".
Archaic ("s'ébaudir" = to be amused); alt spelling esbaudir.
Old-French spelling variant of ébaudir.
Dubious back-formation from the noun "accalmie"; verify this is actually attested as a verb before generating rows.
Archaic variant of fleurir; confirms that florissait/florissaient (see skip_artifact entries below) are inflected forms of this same verb, not independent gaps.
Archaic/defective ("venir a chevir" = to manage/cope); no real full paradigm.
NOT actually re+avoir by simple prefix-stripping (starts "ra-" not "re-"); standard grammars treat it as usable essentially only in the infinitive.
entre + apercevoir with vowel elision (entre+apercevoir -> entrapercevoir); apercevoir/decevoir/concevoir all share Verbiste's dé:cevoir template.
Archaic ("faire assavoir" = to make known); loosely tied to savoir's template but usage is limited to a few fixed forms.
Archaic/legal ("to appear in court"); highly defective. Not simply comparaître's template (different verb shape) -- no confident template assignment.

Possibly é + perdre (source of the adjective "éperdu"); perdre uses Verbiste's ten:dre template, so this would follow it too, but not fully certain this is a real independent verb rather than an adjective-only lemma.
Archaic infinitive of courir, survives only in "chasse a courre"; defective.
Archaic ("to portray", source of "portrait"); traire/extraire/distraire all share Verbiste's extra:ire template.
Defective, only used as "faire accroire"; croire's cr:oire template applies to whatever limited forms exist.

To kill (archaic/humorous); genuinely idiosyncratic conjugation (occis, occira, occise) not shared with any other Verbiste-covered verb family found so far -- needs its own hand-built template rather than reuse.
re + apprendre with vowel elision (re+apprendre -> rapprendre); apprendre uses Verbiste's pr:endre template.
Archaic ("to burn", source of "ardent"); effectively obsolete, no real modern paradigm.
Shares the concl:ure template with conclure/exclure even though bare "clure" is not itself a Verbiste entry.
entre + battre (no elision, just missing from a naive hyphenated-prefix match); battre's bat:tre template applies directly.
entre + clore; note éclore uses a different Verbiste template (éclo:re) than clore (cl:ore) -- this should follow clore's, not éclore's.
Archaic/legal ("perdre par égarement", source of "adiré"); not actually derived from "dire" despite the surface resemblance -- its own defective verb, no confident template.
Parallel formation to descendre, which uses Verbiste's ten:dre template; only descendre/perdre-family members confirmed so far, treat with some caution.
